hints: Use the sector area formula $\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2}r^2\theta$ with $r = 4\text{ cm}$ and $\text{Area} = 10\text{ cm}^2$.
walkthrough:
Apply the area formula for a circular sector of radius $r = 4\text{ cm}$:
$$\text{Area}(\text{sector } ABD) = \frac{1}{2}r^2 \angle BAD = 10$$

Substitute $r = 4$ and solve for $\angle BAD$ in radians:
$$\frac{1}{2}(4^2)\angle BAD = 10 \implies 8\angle BAD = 10 \implies \angle BAD = \frac{10}{8} = 1.25\text{ radians}$$

ai_rubric.Area of a Sector: Sets $\frac{1}{2}(4^2)\angle BAD = 10$ (M1). Solves to obtain $\angle BAD = 1.25\text{ rad}$ (A1).

hints: Calculate opposite side $BC = 4\tan(1.25)$ in right $\triangle ABC$.
Sum $BD + BC + CD$ to find the total perimeter.
walkthrough:
Calculate the length of the circular arc $BD$ using $s = r\theta$:
$$\text{Arc } BD = 4 \times 1.25 = 5\text{ cm}$$

In the right-angled triangle $\triangle ABC$, calculate the length of side $BC$:
$$BC = AB\tan(\angle BAD) = 4\tan(1.25) \approx 4(3.0096) \approx 12.038\text{ cm}$$

Calculate the hypotenuse $AC$ and the segment length $CD$ (where radius $AD = 4\text{ cm}$):
$$AC = \frac{AB}{\cos(\angle BAD)} = \frac{4}{\cos(1.25)} \approx \frac{4}{0.3153} \approx 12.685\text{ cm}$$
$$CD = AC - AD = 12.685 - 4 = 8.685\text{ cm}$$

Sum the three boundary lengths to find the perimeter of the shaded region:
$$\text{Perimeter} = \text{Arc } BD + BC + CD = 5 + 12.038 + 8.685 = 25.723 \approx 25.7\text{ cm}$$

ai_rubric.Perimeter of Circular Shapes: Calculates arc $BD = 5\text{ cm}$ (M1). Calculates $BC \approx 12.04\text{ cm}$ (M1). Calculates $CD \approx 8.69\text{ cm}$ (M1). Obtains perimeter $= 25.7\text{ cm}$ (A1).
